nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a finite field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. Then $v(x) = 1$ for every nonzero $x \in K$.
nodes.title: Absolute values on finite fields are trivial

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$, $w$ real-valued absolute values on $K$. The topologies induced on $K$ by $v$ and by $w$ are equal if and only if $v$ and $w$ are equivalent.
nodes.title: Absolute values inducing the same topology are equivalent

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. The topology induced by $v$ on $K$ is the topology pulled back along the identity map from $K$ to $K$ equipped with the norm $v$; equivalently, it is the metric topology of the distance $d(x, y) = v(x - y)$ on $K$.
nodes.title: Topology induced by an absolute value

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. Then $v$ is nonarchimedean, that is, $v(x + y) \le \max(v(x), v(y))$ for all $x, y \in K$, if and only if $v(n) \le 1$ for every positive integer $n$, viewed as the element $n \cdot 1$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Nonarchimedean criterion using positive integers

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. Then $v$ is nonarchimedean, that is, $v(x + y) \le \max(v(x), v(y))$ for all $x, y \in K$, if and only if $v(n) \le 1$ for every natural number $n$, viewed as the element $n \cdot 1$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Nonarchimedean criterion for absolute values

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Then every real-valued absolute value $v$ on $K$ is nonarchimedean: $v(x + y) \le \max(v(x), v(y))$ for all $x, y \in K$.
nodes.title: Absolute values in positive characteristic are nonarchimedean

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. If $v(n) \le 1$ for every natural number $n$, viewed as the element $n \cdot 1$ of $K$, then $v$ is nonarchimedean: $v(x + y) \le \max(v(x), v(y))$ for all $x, y \in K$.
nodes.title: Absolute values bounded by one on the natural numbers are nonarchimedean

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring, $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $R$ and $c$ a real number with $0 < c \le 1$. The $c$-th power of $v$ takes the value $v(x)^c$ at every $x \in R$.
nodes.title: Values of a power of an absolute value

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring, $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $R$ and $c$ a real number with $0 < c \le 1$. The $c$-th power of $v$ is the real-valued absolute value $x \mapsto v(x)^c$ on $R$.
nodes.title: Powers of an absolute value

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
